name: task-112-lazy-rerank-ab-intel-local
comment: Task 112 lazy heap-f32 rerank A/B. NON-STANDARD config (justified): the canonical lane sweep does not carry a heap-f32 coarse_rerank index nor a lazy-on/lazy-off A/B, which is exactly what this gate needs. Two matched IVF indexes per scale built with storage_format='coarse_rerank', rerank='heap_f32', rerank_format='f32', rerank_placement='table' (the surface Task 112 touches). The recall/latency steps run the standard ec_ivf nprobe default_sweep [8,16,24,32,48,64] (profiles.rs) verbatim. The A/B is driven by the per-step session_guc ec_ivf.lazy_heap_rerank = on|off; everything else is held fixed so recall, ordering, and counters are directly comparable. NOTE: under the sound NoBound contract that holds until Task 113 lands a calibrated lower bound, lazy==fixed by construction (skipped==0), so this run is expected to show byte-identical recall/ordering and EQUAL heap rows/blocks/latency between the two arms. It exists to (a) confirm the gate is wired and recall-neutral on a real corpus, and (b) become the live win-measurement the moment Task 113 supplies a bound that lets the stop fire. ENV-BLOCKED on this dev/review box (no staged corpora at data/staged-current/, no ecaz binary); run on the Intel bench desktop after staging ec_real_100k.
